review_text: My wife and I went to eat here based on yelp reviews, and we are so glad we did. We didn't have a bad bite to eat. We had the black bass, hamachi, eggs & caviar, hens of the forest (mushrooms), and swordfish. I won't describe the dishes, as other reviewers have done that very well (Katya D.) Everything was amazing, food-wise, as well as the service. We sat at the bar, and Andy (head chef) was great at explaining what we were eating and how he came up with the dish. He was really friendly, humble, and made the experience that much better. When he found out we were there to celebrate an anniversary, he even whipped up a dessert for us, on the house. It is great when you are able to find these hidden gems, where you go in not knowing what to expect, but then getting blown away when you do. One of the more memorable meals I have had, and I have been to several of the great restaurants in the city, so that is saying something. Most importantly, my wife also had a great time. We are definitely coming back to sample some more of the menu. You will not be disappointed.

I came here for an early dinner and drinks with colleagues on a business trip. Service is pretty fast. The place was pretty lively and busy.  Interesting decorations; we were seated next to a bunch of miniature wall figures. I had the chipotle chicken tacos. The portion size was pretty small so try something else or get another order with it if you want a bigger meal. Still, they were very tasty and had a nice mild flavor to them. I'd recommend this place as a casual, lively place to come get a drink and enjoy a relaxed time out.
Positive: Good food, decent lunch special price Negative: uncomfortable seats, small parking lot

Little Owl might be one of the cutest restaurants in West Village and possibly in all of New York. We made a reservation before we found ourselves in the cozy restaurant, happily sheltered from the humid and rainy New York weather. After having perused the menu, we decided to split an order of the meatball sliders, the ricotta ravioli and the lamb fillet. Not too long after, the sliders and the ravioli arrived. I'll admit, I was a little shocked by the size of everything. The sliders are mini-sliders. I was able to hold a slider in between my thumb and forefinger. But the taste made up for everything. The buns were soft, the marinara had the slightest bit of zest and the meatballs were spiced and flavorful and juicy. As for the ravioli, the sauce was once again tangy and complimentary and the ravioli was toothsome and not too rich. Then the lamb fillet came. Unsurprisingly, this was rather small too. But it was good. And crispy. And full of lamby goodness. The side veggies were quite delicious as well. Overall, I am glad I went to Little Owl. The service was great, the food was good and the atmosphere was quaint and homey. The cost of our meal, however, was another story. For four tiny sliders, four little raviolis and two small slabs of lamb, the total came out to about $60. Not the cheapest meal we've had, obviously.   But I regret nothing!!

I still really like Istanbul cafe. However, I've found that when I want Turkish food now (which is pretty often because it's AWESOME!), I choose to go to Saray in West Haven. Not only is it cheaper, but also BYOB, which is just about my favorite thing in the entire world. Peace.

Yelp, you are usually so good to me. You're like an old friend that I know well and who knows me. You've been with me through many moves and visits to different cities. You've saved me from potentially disastrous hair cuts and pointed me in the right direction to some truly excellent food. But Yelp - you let me down on this one. NOTE: Cash only A 45 minute wait in a crowded bar next to Supper Restaurant. When I say crowded I mean I was the barback handing bottles to the bartender from a bus boy who couldn't get through the room. Seated about an hour later in the back room of the restaurant. Snotty crowd who made it difficult to get to our table in the corner. Bus boy who shouted out the options "Tap or spawkling?!". Our waiter seemed genuinely Italian, the 3rd seating of the night moved in quickly with a couple of large groups. The music (as with most restaurants in New York) was 80's and 90's and was way too loud. That plus the cackling of the 10 top next to us - forget it - I'll talk to you after dinner. Drinks arrived after our pasta dinners were served. Whereas I admire a timely service, making me feel like you've got a stop watch until you can turn my table is rude buddy. I just wanted to finish my bolognese and get out of there. Had to run to the ATM at the corner store on the same block. Won't be back.

Im happy to see the hipster influence in Astoria now spreading westward towards my grandparents old broadway and 46th street stomping grounds. I had a late lunch here with the girlfriend on a rainy weekday and we were overall pretty pleased with the outcome of our decision. A grilled cheese place with some style. An eclectic menu that can satisfy the easiest of cravings with some original and innovating dishes from simple cores. Didnt get much of a thrill from the soups or salads but as side pieces they were fine. The atmosphere makes for a nice changes coming off of a very busy and dirty steinway. I'll definitely hit this place up again when im on the other side of steinway.

Better than the sum of its parts.   When I think of August, there really isn't anything that's incredibly special.  The food is impeccably prepared, but there's nothing on the menu that's really special.  The atmosphere and decor is really pleasant, but it's not spectacular.  The service is always solid, but there's no fawning over you.  The pricing is reasonable for the quality of the food, but it's not cheap, nor is this a spot where the food is impressive due to it's poundage.  But when it all comes together what you get is an amazingly pleasant and satisfying dining experience.  Isn't that what you want when you go out to eat? I've eaten there about a dozen times since it opened.  Once on a busy night we, like some other reviewers, had to wait about 20 minutes for our reserved table.  But it's a small, intimate, restaurant, and that can happen with second seating's.  The portions aren't huge, then again, this isn't an Applebees.  Take the scallops: typically 3 large scallops over a bed of flavorful greens for $8, if I remember correctly, but they are done to absolute perfection, soft with just a hint of browning on the surface.  Dinner for two will run you over $100 with tip if you do a couple of appetizers, your entrees, desert (they're all good), sparkling water, and cappuccino.  That does put August in some serious competition in Philly, but it more than holds its own.  I'm booked for dinner there again, tonight.

I have heard sooo many good things about this spot! Unfortunately I give it a 2 star because of the service. Let me give you a run down right quick PROS: Lovely area! Makes you want to buy a bike with a basket and put a little yorkipoo in it! Food was okay. I ordered pancakes with sausage (nasty) and hashbrowns...which the hashbrowns were BOMB! Pancakes really tasted homemade and light...sadly I love ihops pancakes way better. YIKES! CONS: The hostest was really nice but thats not what made the experience bad...She was OVERLY nice...so nice we waited an hour and some change to be seated and the place wasnt super packed as expected! There was a group of women who finished there meal about 10 min ago and was just sitting there talking about how lonely and single they are (im sure). The hostest asurres me that their tap is being rung up and we should be seated in 10 min. Kool...but then 20 min pass by...and I ask politely if there getting up soon. She said o yes they are.....OKAY 45 min go by and my friend walks in there and tempts to ask the group of ladies nicely when will they be done?...but before she could finish...the hostest said "They'll be done when there ready" WTF!? How rude of her to let paying customers who have been so patient wait for overly talkative women just sit there like their the only freaking people in the world!..I think the hostest should have politely told the group another party is waiting to be seated. She was waaaay to nice in letting them just sit there. She had no balls to tell them to get their butts up!.....but since she told my friend "they'll be done when their ready" was an invitation for the group to chill longer..which they did!!! No way! With that said....I dont care much to go back....food wasn't all that. ihop NEXT STOP!

I love this place! I hope they never leave. I've been there about 12 times already. Staff is awesome & the food, the coffee & the deserts,  are delicious. My  personal FAVORITE, the Chorizo MAC N Cheese!!! You have to find out when they have it on the menu first. I haven't heard 1 person say they didn't like it. The fish & chips? YUM! Oh & the sauce that comes with the fries. Can't even tell you whats in it but everyone should try it at least once!  The pork, the roast beef! Yum Yum! I've tried alot of their foods and I have yet to be disappointed. They have WI-FI, & it's a relaxing atmosphere with a fireplace (electric one) & good music . Oh 1 more important thing. They Cater! Had my Superbowl party catered and a friend of mine had a huge party catered too. I can tell you people at both parties were very pleased!!!!

I use to live in Jersey City right around the corner from the original Taqeria Downtown. When I moved to the city I started having cravings for their tacos and was considering making a special trip to Jersey City to have them again (Yes, they are that good). But I found out that they recently opened a new location on the lower east side so I set out to find it. Like the Jersey City location, this spot is located in a small space with limited seating so you may have to wait a few minutes to get a table. Once you are seated, someone promptly takes your order and brings a basket of chips and salsa. The chips and salsaa was a nice addition as the Taqeria in JC did not serve chips and salsa. I ordered my favorite tacos, one steak taco and one pork taco, with a side of creama. The tacos where just as I remembered them. The steak taco comes with a spicy salsa on top while the pork comes with a mild green salsa. Both are topped with cilantro and onion and garnished with a raddish and lime wedge. Squeze the lime on the tacos and add a little creama and you have two of the best tasting, authentic tacos you can find. YUM! Highly recommended.

Popular and busy with tourists on Saturday night, surprisingly the food was very good (Northern Italian cooking mostly). the prices were on the high side - but that is Manhattan... Parking is very tight around the narrow local streets (so narrow that our car's side mirror was clipped off by a passing car...) good reviews (Zagat "best Italian restaurant in little Italy"); Service was friendly and attentive, place was fairly modern-tacky and clean. Coming from the suburbs, I had better Italian food at lower prices, - but, again, that is Manhattan.

Affordable good food. Their prices are very reasonable & if you're looking for a quick bite this is your place.  Just careful not to drip any sauce on your coat.  I was really enjoying my chicken sandwich that I noticed all the sauce has dripped down all over my coat.  I didn't like the falafel it was dry so I tossed it, maybe because I'm spoiled with good falafel & kabobs in LA.
Ok service , and good food but bit pricey .
This place was so delicious. My boyfriend and I tried the curry chicken and jerk chicken with cabbage, festival and rice and beans. Highly recommend stopping by and checking it out!

Ehh. Dined there six times. The first time was fun being inside the old bank building. Kind of cool. Food was ok, but pricey. But it seems like the menu rarely changes enough to keep me interested. If I see another one of those oversized white bowls coming out of the kitchen I will fall off my chair. Great restaurants keep innovating, which union league does not. Solid, traditional, boring French food. There are so many better restaurants within a three block radius, why go there more than once? Service ok. Drinks over priced...this isn't nyc fellas. I would say that this is a good choice for a special occasion where the parties have not dined there before. Other than that save your money and go elsewhere.
I was lost in Staten Island stop for direction got great  lunch  and a place for sure I will return too ..(Family Feel) . across for the Staten Island ferry

This place is solid. The food is badass and the drinks are mesmerizing. True beer flows from the taps. If you land on a live music night, you won't be disappointed (unless you hate live music, in which case, you're lost). Very few homeless-looking kids, and even fewer douchebags. I find Cubana to be, in the words of Trent Reznor, a warm place. I only wish it were closer to where I live. Seems to be quite mellow during the week and quite lively on weekends...Schedule to taste.   PS - Don't listen to the fat guy, a Cuban sandwich and some yucca frites will do your stomach right. If not, you haven't finished your Cuba Libre.

i love Nizi Sushi gooood food always packed but its all good. Unfortunately that is in the past now, new owner does not served the same quality of food like what they used to have.  Sorry Guys...wish you the best thou
The outdoor patio is prime real estate for happy hour, take it from me the St Gin cocktail & all their martinis are to die for!

My husband I and rented out the restaurant for our wedding ceremony and reception. Everything was fabulous! The food was delicious and plentiful and the atmosphere was lively. Our favorites: the platanos rellenos and the chipoltle corn crusted salmon- delicious! For dessert we offered churros and flan..

I decided to stop by Rumbamba around 6:15 PM with the thought that since the Ay Arepa food cart on York Street was closing soon I would just stop by the restaurant and get the ingredients fresh. Big mistake! There was only one difference between my food cart fish arepa and the restaurant fish arepa - PRICE! While I can grab a fish arepa from the food cart for 6$, I was charged 13$ for a takeout fish arepa. The portion size was the same (good) and the flavors were the same (delicious!), however I now know that I should always choose the food cart above physical location. If you don't mind shelling out the extra money, the food is delicious. I can't speak to the dining conditions since my meal was takeout.
Great restaurant, really good food and low prices. We love the place, and I love their red curry in particular. The only negative is that there can be a pretty long wait at times to get seated.

Istanbul Cafe offers some great Turkish specialties. The imam bayildi, baba ganoush, iskender kebab, and patlican musakka are excellent places to start if you're not as familiar with Turkish cuisine. My primary issues with Istanbul are that the service can be slow when it's crowded and that their lighting is incredibly dim. It almost feels like you're eating in a cave. That said, I'd still recommend the food highly. Even if you don't feel like dining in the restaurant, they're very prompt with takeout orders and the quality/quantity of what they give you is just as good.

a neighborhood gem...Delicious grilled calimari, fresh salads,  perfectly prepared risotto, flavorful and balanced pastas, thoughtful and carefully selected wine list at modest prices, and richly chocolate dolci. Everything we ate was fully flavored and freshly prepared. A wonderful meal for any day of the week.

Being from Miami, and visiting NY I can say that these are one of the worst empanadas I've had. Not authentic what so ever, and the service was terrible. Not worth waiting in line to try this place out
yes. especially if you're visiting and just out for a walk. class, character, and a good product. I will return.

Known as the place where lots of Yale grad students and professors will go for pizza, I've had pizza delivered from here a few times. Unfortunately, it failed to impress. The pizza had a bit of a cardboard consistency to it and the tomato sauce was too bland. You can do a lot better in New Haven.

I am SO happy to have a BBQ place in Fort Greene that's better than the mediocre Smoke Joint. While this place might not be the most consistent every time, when it's good (which is most of the time) it hits it out of the park. The pork ribs are excellent, the chicken is great... sides are delicious too. There a cute patio out in back as well. I hope it sticks around because the location's a bit off the beaten track of Myrtle. Please support this place!!!!

I came here with my boyfriend on a Monday afternoon (around 1:30pm) and we were seated right away. The place was a lot smaller than I expected it to be so be prepared to sit very close to the party next to you. The guys making the pizza are at the back of the restaurant and you can actually watch them work with the dough, toppings, and the coal oven which is pretty nice. PRICE - pretty decent for a whole pie, we ordered a small with two toppings and a soda for under $20 PIZZA - I must say that I first experienced the thin crust, authentic pizza at Lombardi's in lower manhattan and expected much more from Grimaldi's. Reading the raging reviews, I thought Grimaldi's might take the lead as my favorite pizza joint but it didn't cut it. The crust was good but the bottom wasn't as crispy as the ones from Lombardi's and the selection of toppings was definitely not up to par with the selection Lombardi's provides. Nonetheless, it was definitely enjoyable on a cold winter day and it was definitely better than a regular pizzeria. Grimaldi's is a very casual and laid-back restaurant and the staff is friendly. All NYC natives should stop by at least once and you can tell that many tourists make an effort to make a trip here as well. However, as we were leaving the restaurant, a short line as already formed outside so I guess we lucked out with the waiting in the cold!
Very friendly owners.  Decor is dated but the food is so delicious.  Do not let the decor distract you because it is so tasty and cooked fresh.

Decent enough, I'd say.  Especially if you're used to eating Subway's meatball sandwich (which I am VERY guilty of).  I don't think it's really worth waiting in line.  Especially when you're drunk.  Meatball Shop is definitely quite scene-y then.  If you know where to get a good meatball sandwich or dish, well, you won't really think anything special of this place.  I do know where to get a good meatball -- hint - any Italian deli in Brooklyn.  And Ferdinando's in the Columbia Street Waterfront District.  Overall, I don't really have that many complaints with this spot.  I just know there are better places and for less.

Grilled Corn Mexican Style served with mayonnaise, cotija cheese (hard cow's milk cheese that originated from Mexico. It is named after the town of Cotija, Michoacán), chili (sic)powder and lime by two thanks. That is all you need to know about this place.

This place is a hidden gem! Have been frequenting Roberto's for two years now and have had a great experience every time (for both take-out and dining). Authentic Italian cuisine (so incredibly delicious and better than many other more popular Italian restaurants in the city), fast and friendly service, as well as a great atmosphere. Portions here aren't overwhelming like many Italian restaurants, which some people might complain about, but that's because their focus is more on the taste... and believe me, everything I have tried here so far has been tasty. Only downside is that they don't deliver, but then I would probably be ordering from them every other day. Also, their valentine's day fixed menu is especially yummy!

The restaurant itself is cute and trendy. I would have to say the food is just ok. Stay away from the Fettuccine with Rock Shrimp & Lobster Broth. It is EXTREMELY disappointing. We also got the buffalo mozzarella and grilled tomato salad; cannot believe they charge $13 for this. It just wasn't very good. Two things I really enjoyed were the falafel crusted scallops and the hanger steak. Overall, food was not worth the prices. If you want a place with nice ambience and don't mind overpaying on mediocre food this is definitely the place.
it is not good place

My father lives in Taiwan so I grew up eating Taiwanese/Chinese food.  I find the quality and deliciousness of Formosa's food unsurpassed by any other Chinese restaurant in CT.  I often order takeout for easy dinner parties and all of my friends rave about it and make me feel like champion for very little effort.
BYOB is dangerous because my friends and I always get too drunk, which leads to us getting shushed at and ruining date nights. It also makes the food 10Xs better.

We came to New York on a family holiday trip. My husbands family are Italians from upstate New York. We heard how fantastic it was and decided to try it. This is one of the best places I have ever eaten....EVER. I recommend every entree-we were with a huge party and I tried it all. Don't miss the tiramisu or the ricotta cheesecake! We will be back!!!!

My family and I eat here frequently, and I thought that it is about time that I write a review. We really love this place - the food, the people and the place. We have never had anything that wasn't good, and not infrequently have dishes that are exceptional. I am a Caesar Salad lover, and Pulcinella's version is my absolute favorite. The pizza is wonderful, and compares favorably with what I had when I worked in Milan, Italy. I don't order many entrees myself, but other folks that I dine with do, and they are always satisfied and often enthusastic. Finally, the desserts are great and it is always exciting to try the new offerings. Handicap access is top-notch, which is important to us. We often eat here before concerts at the Flynn, as we can get in and out without any hassle. The bottom line - we love Pulcinella's!
